A0225.title: Physical-World Prompt Injection Detection
A0225.definition: Detection of physical-world prompt-injection attacks against embodied-intelligence VLA models via environment-consistency checking, anomalous-visual-cue identification, and action-intent auditing.
A0225.description:
Physical-world prompt injection detection addresses attacks where the attacker places visual cues (stickers, printed patterns, occluders, projections) in the robot's working environment to induce the VLA model to misread instructions; it builds detection capability across three dimensions. First, environment-consistency checking compares instructions parsed by the VLM against registered legitimate instruction sources (operator voice/text/predefined tasks), downweighting or rejecting instructions of unknown origin. Second, anomalous-visual-cue identification detects suspicious injectioncarrier such as high-contrast text suddenly appearing, unnaturally arranged patterns, and signs unrelated to the task. Third, action-intent auditing verifies before the VLA outputs an action sequence whether it matches the current task context and safety boundaries, triggering secondary confirmation for actions deviating from expected intent.

This measure is key to embodied intelligence versus pure-software prompt-injection defense; because the injectioncarrier exists in the physical world, pure input filtering cannot eradicate it, requiring defense-in-depth combining environment perception and action-layer verification. It complements A0178 (AIoT model security protection) and A0014 (tamper-proofing).
A0225.limitation: Hard to enumerate all injection forms; novel adversarial examples can bypass detectors; dynamic physical environments (lighting, occlusion, viewpoint) cause high false-positive rates; the detector itself may be adversarially attacked; real-time requirements versus detection overhead make deployment difficult in all scenarios.
